```
$ TMPDIR=/tmp PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=scripts python3 -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/tests/test_outcome_score_f002.py -q

$ TMPDIR=/tmp PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=scripts python3 -c '<read-only score_plan census over docs/plans/*>'
$ sed -i '' 's/_ac3_plan(/_accepted_gap_plan(/g' scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/tests/test_outcome_score_f002.py
```

I read the three prior codex audits first and confirmed the scoring behaviour the rewritten acceptance asks for was already implemented at i2 and is untouched by the D010 split — the third route (a feature carrying `{metric ≥10, method ∈ walk|request|named_test|probe}` IS a slice), the refusal firing only when no outcome is reachable by any route, and the absent-audience gap being recorded rather than refused — so I changed no production code and left `close_obligations()`/`read_score_sidecar()` alone for F004/F005. What was genuinely stale was the acceptance→test mapping: the suite still carried the pre-split five-criterion numbering, so tests named `test_ac3_*`/`test_ac5_*` with docstrings claiming those ACs were actually proving
